title: Prove the work safely
learning_outcome: Package scoped proof and test an idea without leaking the underlying record.
exercise: Redact a fictional trace and score a mock app concept against the workflow.

boundaries.evidence: No client data, private screenshots, or public claims of deployment.
boundaries.privacy: synthetic Harbor only; no actual participant, client, admin, or private corpus content
boundaries.authority: prepare_only; no live agent, memory promotion, message, booking, spending, or publication

scenes.narration_exact: “A fictional Harbor board member asks Morgan what the preparation agent actually did for the proposed session. Morgan could hand over the entire trace. That would reveal source notes and internal deliberation the board member did not request. Morgan could write a polished story from memory. That would be hard to check. We need a smaller packet: enough to show the boundary, the work, the hold, and the human decision, without dragging every underlying record into the room.”

scenes.narration_exact: “Chapter Twenty-One's Scoped Proof Loop has six fields: audience, scope, window, exclusions, export, and ledger. For our invented board reader, scope is one Harbor session-option paper case, across one fictional planning window. Include the permitted job, evidence-status summary, handoff result, `SYN-HOLD-01`, Morgan's paper disposition, and the still-unapproved `SYN-SPEND-01`. Exclude raw source text, prompts, private reasoning, unrelated people, and any actual records. The packet records what is known and what is withheld. It does not certify agent quality or imply a session happened.”

scenes.narration_exact: “The same team then hears an idea: a tiny phone tool that helps volunteer coordinators compare workshop options. The temptation is to build it because it fits the Harbor story. Chapter Twenty-Two asks for a Foundry Test first: demand, monetization, builder fit, build velocity, differentiation, release readiness, and approval gates. The workbook proposes a weighted score out of one hundred. A score is useful only when each field has attributable evidence. Our class has no real market research, payer interview, or release review. Those fields stay unscored. A made-up number would turn an idea into false proof.”
scenes.on_screen_copy_exact: “Idea → evidence → packet → human gate.” “Missing evidence: unscored.”

scenes.narration_exact: “Write the smallest safe next test: Morgan could ask for permission to research public demand and clarify who would pay. Even that is a proposed plan, not a provider call or outreach. No repository, tester invite, user data collection, price, store listing, or public claim follows from this lesson. A phone can display the packet and a hold status, but it cannot waive the gate. The valuable outcome may be a decision to shelve the idea. That saves time a rushed build would consume.”

scenes.narration_exact: “Draft a Client-Safe Proof Packet outline for the single Harbor planning case. State audience, scope, window, inclusions, exclusions, export review, and ledger fields. Redact the fictional trace in words rather than pasting it. Then make a Foundry Test for the volunteer-coordinator tool: mark each evidence field observed, missing, or unscored; name a payer question, a tiny proposed test, the human gate, and a stop condition. Use only invented case material. Do not fetch private records, contact a person, create a repo, or generate a public claim.”
scenes.on_screen_copy_exact: Exercise card below; 3:20 quiet writing timer with optional pause.
scenes.exercise_prompt_exact: Create a `Client-Safe Proof Packet` outline for one fictional Harbor decision with audience, scope, window, capability and delegation boundary, trace references, approval/hold history, spend authority summary, exclusions, export review owner, and ledger metadata. Then create a `Foundry Test` for one adjacent app idea. For each field, name its evidence or mark it `unscored`; include demand, payer/monetization, builder fit, build velocity, differentiation, release readiness, approval gates, the smallest proposed test, and stop condition. Do not substitute a fabricated total score for missing evidence.
